framework_title: Biomagnetic Walk: Transport, Selection, and Phase Null Explorer
central_question: Can a proposed field-dependent biological response be distinguished from spatial selection, growth effects, shared forcing, and model-imposed coupling?
architectural_separation: Independent hypothesis-first research prototype repository separate from aurascoper/oklo_shareable_portal and aurascoper/Biofilms. Organizes the material around (1) Three Distinct Systems with explicit evidence tags (OBSERVED, OBSERVED_IN_VITRO, MODELED, HYPOTHESIZED, UNRESOLVED_TRANSDUCTION, ENGINEERED, CONTEXT-DEPENDENT, QUARANTINED), (2) the 4-Proposition Main Causal Gap (P1 -> P2 -> P3 -> P4), and (3) the Biomagnetic Walk: Transport, Selection, and Phase Null Explorer testing Null H0-A (no active parcel displacement), Null H0-B (selection-only survivor shift), and Phase Coupling Controls across Gates 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4.

channel_separation_principle.radiation_channel: Spatial radiation dose gradient (grad I_gamma, keV-MeV ionizing photons/particles) acts as an energy, radiolytic/redox, and position-dependent mortality/selection input channel.
channel_separation_principle.magnetic_channel: Magnetic flux density vector B (25 to 65 uT geomagnetic or mT engineered) acts as a directional spin-chemistry or mechanical torque information channel.
channel_separation_principle.selection_vs_movement_principle: An outward shift in the surviving biomass distribution does not establish outward movement: in cpm-sp-v1 (source 841d052, 256 seeds), dose-dependent mortality removes 5,511 of 10,752 parcels near the axis, shifting survivor mean radius outward by up to +0.0493 r/R while every identified-parcel displacement interval delta_r_i = r_i(t_1) - r_i(t_0) spans zero.

null_hypotheses.title: Null H0-A: No Active Directional Movement (Individual Parcel Trajectory Invariance)
null_hypotheses.statement: The magnetic field or radiation gradient changes parcel survival or growth, but does not alter the movement or directional-growth rule of an individual identifiable parcel.
null_hypotheses.statistic: delta_r_i = r_i(t_1) - r_i(t_0) computed for the same identifiable parcel i across time; parcel disappearances (deaths/commitments) are logged as separate selection events and never silently dropped without reporting evaluable/excluded counts.
null_hypotheses.rejection_criterion: Requires the paired/sham-contrasted distribution of identified-parcel displacements delta_r_i to exclude zero outside the preregistered MEOI bound. A shift in the surviving population's mean radius does NOT reject H0-A.

null_hypotheses.title: Null H0-B: Apparent Spatial Shift Is Explained by Selection Alone
null_hypotheses.statement: The endpoint spatial distribution of biomass is fully explained by position-dependent survival, division, or parcel removal (mortality near the source axis), without any active directional transport.
null_hypotheses.statistic: Contrast between observed survivor mean radius r_surv(t_1) and the initial radius r_surv(t_0) of those same surviving parcels (plus the fixed-position selection counterfactual where movement is disabled).
null_hypotheses.rejection_criterion: Requires a reproducible discrepancy between the observed endpoint distribution and a selection-only counterfactual that preserves initial positions and applies measured position-dependent survival/growth rates.

cpm_sp_v1_growth_off_256_seeds.description: Growth OFF, 256 seeds (42..297), N=40, 6 parcels/species (10,752 total parcels), MCS 100, synthetic clock 60 s/MCS, axis dose rate 0.01 Gy/s, 95% seed-bootstrap intervals (5,000 samples, seed 9004).

phase_locking_and_controls.synthetic_parameters: Mean period 20 MCS, Normal frequency SD 0.05 rad/MCS, coupling K = 0.5 / MCS; phase never feeds back into nonphase quantities.

growth_off_v1_summary.interpretation: On the fragmented growth-off contact graph (~10-11 components, ~5 isolates), K = 0.5 narrows frequency spread inside components but produces 0 / 256 global locking within 50-100 MCS.

growth_on_v3_summary.finite_window_locking: 15 / 16 (in both phase_only and combined; Seed 44 fails 0.5 rad range bound at 0.755 rad phase_only / 0.848 rad combined)
growth_on_v3_summary.interpretation: With growth, division fills the lattice into a single connected component (1 component, 0 isolates) and explicit coupling K = 0.5 locks 15 of 16 seeds. All parameters are synthetic; this establishes model-coupling robustness, NOT biological synchronization.

three_required_phase_controls.title: Control 1: Uncoupled Model Replay (K = 0 Counterfactual)
three_required_phase_controls.design: Disable inter-parcel phase coupling (K = 0) while holding recorded parcel membership, initial phases, natural frequencies, and daughter phase inheritance identical.
three_required_phase_controls.finding: In cpm-sp-growth-v1, comparing K = 0.5 against the exact K = 0 replay shows a 98.2% median reduction in effective-frequency spread, proving that the 15/16 phase convergence is driven by the explicit K = 0.5 coupling term on the connected contact graph rather than daughter inheritance alone.

three_required_phase_controls.title: Control 2: Phase-Randomized & Cross-Seed Surrogate
three_required_phase_controls.design: Shuffle initial phases or pair phase trajectories across independent seeds to quantify how much apparent phase concentration R(t) arises by finite-sample chance, shared geometry, or common external forcing.
three_required_phase_controls.finding: High R(t) measures phase concentration, not its physical source; cross-seed surrogates separate shared environmental forcing from direct inter-parcel interaction.

three_required_phase_controls.title: Control 3: Preregistered Biological Benchmark vs. Independent-Oscillator Null
three_required_phase_controls.design: Before any biological synchronization claim is permitted, preregister a primary synchronization statistic (e.g., Kuramoto R(t) and locking time distribution) on live-cell reporter time-series and test against an explicit uncoupled-oscillator + lineage-inheritance null model.
three_required_phase_controls.finding: Currently unexecuted in wet lab; all cpm-sp-growth-v1 phase parameters are synthetic.

experimental_design_note.statistical_note: Crossing the five rows with three genotypes yields 15 condition-by-genotype combinations (a planned-contrast design focused on radiation-coupled magnetic manipulations). A fully crossed 24-cell design (2 Radiation states x 4 Magnetic-field states x 3 Genotypes) additionally tests rotated (+90 deg), reversed (180 deg), and suppressed (<0.1 uT) magnetic fields under sham radiation to separate general magnetic effects from radiation-dependent magnetic effects.

multiphysics_and_glmm_architecture.overview: Couples four independently testable layers so that physical transport, viscoelastic biofilm mechanics, candidate magnetic/radiation transduction, and hierarchical statistical inference are never conflated.

layers.title: Layer A: Hydrodynamics & Reactive Transport (Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes)
layers.equation: div(u) = 0; rho*(du/dt + (u.grad)u) = -grad(p) + mu*laplacian(u) - (mu/K_perm)*u; dS/dt + div(u*S) = div(D_S*grad(S)) - r_S(S, X_i)
layers.scope: Couples Navier-Stokes free flow and Darcy-Brinkman porous biofilm flow with nutrient/oxygen/redox-mediator reactive transport, enforcing mass-conservation and grid-convergence checks (< 1e-6 budget residual).
sources: Kim & Yao (2026) A conservative micro-continuum-cellular automaton method for multispecies biofilm dynamics in complex flows (arXiv:2610.01565)

layers.title: Layer B: Microbial Kinetics & Viscoelastic Biofilm Rheology (Oldroyd-B vs. Generalized Newtonian)
layers.equation: dX_i/dt + div(u*X_i) = div(D_i*grad(X_i)) + mu_i*X_i - d_i*X_i + a_i - e_i; T + lambda_1*upper_convected_deriv(T) = 2*eta_0*(D + lambda_2*upper_convected_deriv(D))
layers.scope: Separates species growth (mu_i), position-dependent mortality (d_i, Null H0-B), attachment (a_i), and detachment (e_i) from viscoelastic EPS stress relaxation (lambda_1), storage/loss moduli (G', G''), and detachment under shear. Requires independent rheometric calibration (rheograms) rather than circular fitting from colony geometry.
sources: Charlton et al. (2019) Viscoelastic biofilm streaming and detachment under shear (PMC6707926)
Li, Matous & Nerenberg (2022) Comparing generalized Newtonian and viscoelastic constitutive relations for biofilms (Biotechnol. Bioeng., doi:10.1002/bit.28056)

layers.title: Layer C: Falsifiable Magnetic & Radiation Hypotheses (Explicit Null Parameter theta_i = 0)
layers.equation: mu_i = mu_{i,0}(S, O_2, T) + theta_i * f(B, grad B, I_gamma); v_bias,i = gamma_i * g(B, grad I_gamma); H_0: theta_i = 0, gamma_i = 0
layers.scope: Parameterizes any proposed magnetic or radiation modulation of growth (theta_i), mortality (d_i), or active directional transport (gamma_i) as an explicit perturbation around the null model (theta_i = 0, gamma_i = 0), tested across WT, Melanin-Deficient, and Complemented Rescue strains.
sources: Gassab et al. (2026) Quantum in Biology, Quantum for Biology, and Biology for Quantum (arXiv:2605.00205)

layers.title: Layer D: Hierarchical Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM) Inference
layers.equation: g(E[Y_{ijk}(t)]) = beta_0 + beta_R*R + beta_B*B + beta_M*M + beta_RB*(R*B) + beta_BM*(B*M) + beta_RBM*(R*B*M) + b_batch + b_culture + f(t)
layers.scope: Models treatment effects for Radiation (R), Magnetic manipulation (B: orientation, reversal, suppression), and Melanin genotype (M: WT, Albino, Rescue) while accounting for batch/run random effects (b_batch), biological culture/channel random effects (b_culture), and temporal autocorrelation f(t). Prevents pseudoreplication by never treating pixels, parcels, or time frames as independent biological replicates.
sources: Lee, Green & Ryan (2017) Generalized linear mixed models for clustered/longitudinal biological assay data (arXiv:1709.06288)

endpoint_models.endpoint: Identified-parcel displacement delta_r_i / biomass / modulus G', G''
endpoint_models.model_family: Gaussian / continuous linear mixed model (LMM) with seed/culture random intercepts
Poisson or Negative-Binomial GLMM (log link) accounting for overdispersion

endpoint_models.endpoint: Parcel survival proportion (Null H0-B hazard commitments)
endpoint_models.model_family: Binomial GLMM (logit/complementary log-log link) on surviving vs. initial counts
Longitudinal mixed model with AR(1) / Matérn temporal covariance f(t)
Count / compositional mixed model paired with absolute abundance ledger

decision_gates_0_to_4.title: Gate 0: Verify the Synthetic Model & Conservation Ledgers
decision_gates_0_to_4.scope: Confirm parcel identity tracking across time, initial-state placement balance across arms, explicit death/disappearance event logging (5,511 / 10,752 commitments), nutrient/biomass budget closure (< 1e-6), and restart-exact seed reproducibility (272 / 272 seeds).

verdict_states.PASS: Verified in cpm-sp-v1 and cpm-sp-growth-v1 (source 841d052): 272/272 seeds paired-exact & restart-exact; budgets close to 7.2e-9.
verdict_states.FAIL: Any identity swap, unlogged parcel disappearance, or budget residual > 1e-6 invalidates downstream inference.

decision_gates_0_to_4.title: Gate 1: Displacement vs. Selection (Null H0-A & Null H0-B)
decision_gates_0_to_4.scope: Compare tracked per-parcel trajectories delta_r_i = r_i(t_1) - r_i(t_0) against a selection-only counterfactual (initial radius of survivors + fixed_survival controls). Never infer active movement from surviving parcel locations alone.

verdict_states.PASS_NULL_RETAINED: In cpm-sp-v1 (256 seeds), survivor radius shifts up to +0.0493 r/R, but initial radius of those survivors shifts +0.0538 r/R and all 7 displacement intervals delta_r_i span zero -> H0-A and H0-B retained (selection imitates movement).
verdict_states.REJECT_NULL: Requires tracked delta_r_i to exceed +/-MEOI and diverge significantly from the selection-only counterfactual.

decision_gates_0_to_4.title: Gate 2: Magnetic-Field Null (Orientation, Reversal & Suppression)
decision_gates_0_to_4.scope: Test B-field orientation (+90 deg), reversal (180 deg), and suppression (<0.1 uT) under fixed radiation geometry, active antiparallel sham coils, and 3-axis sample-plane magnetometry.

verdict_states.PASS: Tracked directional vector shifts with B-field rotation/reversal or vanishes under B-suppression relative to sham-energized coils.
verdict_states.NULL_OR_INCONCLUSIVE: No difference across B-field states within equivalence bounds (magnetic null retained), or thermal/vibration sham controls fail.

decision_gates_0_to_4.title: Gate 3: Melanin Dependence vs. Alternative Flavin/Cryptochrome Routes
decision_gates_0_to_4.scope: Use WT, melanin-deficient (albino), and complemented rescue strains across the 5-row factorial matrix to test whether a verified Gate 1/2 response requires melanin (Route A) or persists via cryptochrome/flavin-superoxide spin chemistry (Route B).

verdict_states.ROUTE_A_SUPPORTED: Effect abolished in Albino mutant and restored in Complemented Rescue.
verdict_states.ROUTE_B_SUPPORTED: Magnetic effect persists in Albino mutant and is sensitive to flavin/cryptochrome knockout or wavelength controls.

decision_gates_0_to_4.title: Gate 4: Biochemical Transduction & Temporal Precedence
decision_gates_0_to_4.scope: Measure ROS/redox indicators and mitochondrial state alongside tracked displacement/tip curvature (t_mito < t_tip) and test whether controlled pathway intervention blocks the directional response without arresting normal growth.

verdict_states.PASS: Biochemical shift precedes directional curvature (t_mito < t_tip) AND non-toxic pathway clamp abolishes directional bias while preserving basal extension.
verdict_states.FAIL_BYPRODUCT: ROS/mitochondrial shift occurs only after growth deflection (t_mito >= t_tip) or intervention blocks all growth nonspecifically.

main_causal_gap_propositions.proposition: Melanin changes its redox or paramagnetic radical state under ionizing radiation.
main_causal_gap_propositions.audit_scope: Supported for melanin ESR signal changes and ~4x NADH ferricyanide reduction under irradiation, plus radiation-associated metabolic/growth effects in melanized fungi. Does NOT establish a melanin-mediated magnetic compass.

main_causal_gap_propositions.proposition: Weak magnetic fields alter the relevant spin-dependent radical-pair chemistry.
main_causal_gap_propositions.audit_scope: Photoinduced flavin-tryptophan radical pairs in cryptochrome have experimentally demonstrated magnetic-field-sensitive reaction kinetics and quantum yields in vitro (Maeda et al. 2012; Xu et al. 2021). Flavin-superoxide [FAD*- ... O2*-] radical-pair magnetosensitivity is computationally modeled to reproduce planarian ROS data (Rishabh et al. 2023, arXiv:2312.06597), where the authors explicitly note the model does not establish the mechanism in vivo. Magnetic modulation of fungal melanin radicals remains an untested hypothesis.
sources: Nature Communications (2024) Tightly bound flavin-superoxide radical-pair model

main_causal_gap_propositions.proposition: Spin-dependent chemical yield differences alter mitochondrial or cellular signaling.
main_causal_gap_propositions.audit_scope: Even where radical-pair chemistry is established in vitro, the downstream biological transduction chain from reaction yields through ROS and mitochondrial bioenergetics to cellular polarity requires independent causal evidence at each step.
sources: Gassab et al. (2026) Quantum in Biology, Quantum for Biology, and Biology for Quantum (arXiv:2605.00205)

main_causal_gap_propositions.proposition: Mitochondrial / redox signaling drives reproducible directional fungal hyphal growth (beyond selection H0-B).
main_causal_gap_propositions.audit_scope: Early Chernobyl isolate reports suggested directional growth toward radiation sources, whereas a 2024 Sandia National Laboratories Cs-137 study found no statistically significant growth difference, the aurascoper/Biofilms 256-seed 4-arm movement model is a TOST equivalence null within +/-0.05 r/R, and cpm-sp-v1 demonstrates that dose-gradient mortality shifts survivor radius (+0.0493 r/R) with zero parcel displacement.
sources: Sandia National Laboratories (2024) Cs-137 Fungal Irradiation Report (null result)

default_model_exclusions: Whole-organism magnetic control (not physically or biologically established)
Endogenous ferritin mechanical or thermal channel gating (fails k_B*T and Fourier heat conduction bounds by >4 orders of magnitude; Meister 2016)
Inferring active radiotropism from surviving parcel radius shifts without subtracting position-dependent mortality (Null H0-B; cpm-sp-v1)
Interpreting 15/16 phase locking in cpm-sp-growth-v1 (K = 0.5 synthetic coupling) as evidence of biological synchronization
71 THz (4.22 um mid-IR) mitochondrial light-matter coupling preprint (quarantined as an unvalidated optical/vibrational hypothesis; not geomagnetic sensing)

systems.title: System 1: Biological Response to Radiation (Melanin -> Redox/ROS -> Mitochondria -> Growth vs. Selection)
systems.summary: Evaluates how ionizing radiation interacts with fungal melanin and separates position-dependent survival/selection (Null H0-B) from active directional growth (Null H0-A).

nodes.label: Ionizing Radiation -> Melanin ESR Signal & 4x NADH Reduction
nodes.detail: Continuous ionizing radiation alters melanin electron spin resonance (ESR) paramagnetism and increases melanin-mediated NADH ferricyanide reduction ~4-fold in vitro; melanized fungi show radiation-associated metabolic/growth changes. Does not by itself establish magnetic sensing.
sources: Turick et al. (2002) Appl. Environ. Microbiol. 68:2436-2444
Robertson et al. (2012) PLoS ONE 7(11):e48674 (W. dermatitidis transcriptomics)

nodes.label: Melanin Electron Transfer -> Intracellular Redox / ROS Pool
nodes.detail: Proposed shuttling of radiation-mobilized electrons or radical intermediates from cell-wall/melanosome melanin into cytosolic electron acceptors, superoxide (O2*-), or hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) signaling pools.

nodes.label: Redox / ROS Pool -> Mitochondrial ETC, NAD(P)H & ATP Modulation
nodes.detail: Mitochondria integrate cytosolic redox, calcium, and ROS signals across Complexes I-IV, altering ATP synthesis and stress signaling; direct energy transfer from melanin or spin-pair ROS to mitochondrial ETC in intact hyphae requires temporal ordering and pathway intervention (Gassab et al. 2026).

nodes.label: Survivor Radius Shift (+0.0493 r/R via Selection H0-B) vs. Active Displacement (delta_r_i ~ 0, H0-A)
nodes.detail: In cpm-sp-v1 (256 seeds), axial dose mortality removes 5,511 of 10,752 parcels and shifts survivor radius outward by up to +0.0493 r/R while every identified-parcel displacement interval delta_r_i spans zero. Experimentally, Sandia (2024) found no statistically significant Cs-137 directional growth effect.
sources: Sandia National Laboratories (2024) Cs-137 Fungal Irradiation Report (null result)

systems.title: System 2: Candidate Magnetic Sensing Mechanism (Spin-Chemistry vs. Magnetite Torque)
systems.summary: Evaluates candidate physical transducers capable of sensing weak geomagnetic fields (25 to 65 uT) and distinguishes established in vitro radical-pair spin chemistry from computational superoxide models and untested fungal transduction.

nodes.label: Route A: Melanin Paramagnetic Centers & Radical-Pair Spin Coupling
nodes.detail: Melanin contains stable semiquinone free radicals (detectable by ESR). Route A asks whether weak magnetic fields (B) modulate spin-dependent recombination or electron transfer between melanin radicals and diffusible redox partners.
sources: Dadachova et al. (2007) PLoS ONE 2(5):e457 (melanin ESR paramagnetic signal)

nodes.label: Route B1 (Cryptochrome Flavin-Trp) vs. Route B2 (Flavin-Superoxide [FAD*- ... O2*-] Model)
nodes.detail: Photoinduced flavin-tryptophan radical pairs in cryptochrome have experimentally demonstrated magnetic-field-sensitive reaction kinetics and quantum yields in vitro (Maeda et al. 2012 PNAS; Xu et al. 2021 Nature). Separately, a 2023 computational paper (Rishabh et al. 2023, arXiv:2312.06597) and a 2024 Nature Communications study model flavin-superoxide [FAD*- ... O2*-] radical pairs; Rishabh et al. explicitly state that their model does not establish the mechanism in vivo.
sources: Xu et al. (2021) Nature 594:535-540 (Cry4a in vitro magnetic sensitivity)
Rishabh, Zadeh-Haghighi & Simon (2023) arXiv:2312.06597 (computational flavin-superoxide model)
Nature Communications (2024) Tightly bound flavin-superoxide radical-pair model
Gassab et al. (2026) arXiv:2605.00205 (unresolved biological transduction chain)

nodes.label: Route C: Biogenic Single-Domain Magnetite (Fe3O4) Chain Torque
nodes.detail: Chains of 10 to 20 single-domain Fe3O4 crystals (r ~ 25 nm) achieve mechanical torque tau = N*M_s*V*B*sin(theta) > k_B*T at 50 uT (established in magnetotactic bacteria; eukaryotic mechanoreceptor coupling remains unresolved).

systems.title: System 3: Engineered Magnetic Nanoparticle Interface (Synthetic Actuation vs. Ferritin Bound)
systems.summary: Evaluates synthetic magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs/SPIONs) engineered to stimulate ion channels or target vasculature at millitesla fields, kept strictly separate from natural uT sensing.

nodes.label: Synthetic Fe3O4 Nanodisc / m-Torquer Mechanotransduction (Piezo1 / TRPV4)
nodes.detail: Exogenous synthetic Fe3O4 nanodiscs or torque arrays (35 to 100 nm) under 5 to 50 mT low-frequency fields generate piconewton forces/torques (>10 k_B*T) to gate Piezo1/TRPV4 channels and trigger Ca2+ influx.

nodes.label: RF Magnetothermal Hysteresis Heating (TRPV1 -> Ca2+ -> Mitochondrial MCU)
nodes.detail: Dense synthetic MNP clusters under 100 to 500 kHz RF fields (10 to 30 mT) heat local membranes above 42 C to gate TRPV1, driving Ca2+ uptake into mitochondria via MCU.

nodes.label: Endogenous Ferritin Thermal & Mechanical Failure Bound
nodes.detail: A 6 nm ferrihydrite ferritin core (~300 mu_B) yields tau / (k_B*T) ~ 3.3e-5 at 50 uT and < 1e-2 even at 20 mT, failing thermal noise bounds by >4 orders of magnitude.

mechanisms.title: System 2 (Route B): Cryptochrome Flavin-Trp (In Vitro) & Flavin-Superoxide [FAD*- ... O2*-] (Modeled)
mechanisms.status: CHEMICAL_MAGNETOSENSITIVITY_OBSERVED_IN_VITRO (Maeda 2012; flavin-superoxide MODELED computationally in Rishabh 2023; fungal transduction UNRESOLVED per Gassab 2026)
mechanisms.equation: H_spin = g * mu_B * B . (S_1 + S_2) + sum_i S_1 . A_1i . I_1i; f_L = 1.40 MHz at 50 uT
mechanisms.typical_regime: B = 25 to 65 uT (geomagnetic inclination compass); links spin singlet-triplet yield to ROS / O2*- pool
sources: Xu et al. (2021) Nature 594:535-540 (European robin Cry4a in vitro magnetic sensitivity)
Rishabh, Zadeh-Haghighi & Simon (2023) arXiv:2312.06597 (computational flavin-superoxide model; does not establish mechanism in vivo)
Nature Communications (2024) Tightly bound flavin-superoxide radical-pair geomagnetic sensitivity model
Gassab et al. (2026) arXiv:2605.00205 & Lam & Malkemper (2026) Physiol. Rev. (doi:10.1152/physrev.00032.2025)
unresolved_questions: Maintaining spin relaxation time T_1, T_2 >= 1 us against fast rotational tumbling of free superoxide
Unresolved biological transduction chain from spin-dependent reaction yields to fungal hyphal polarity (Gassab et al. 2026)

mechanisms.title: System 1 + 2 (Route A): Melanin ESR Paramagnetism (Observed) vs. Magnetic Compass (Hypothesized)
mechanisms.status: RADIATION_REDOX_OBSERVED_IN_MELANIZED_FUNGI (Dadachova 2007; melanin-mediated magnetic sensing HYPOTHESIZED; colony radiotropism CONTEXT-DEPENDENT)
mechanisms.equation: I_gamma -> Melanin [Q / QH* / QH2] (4x NADH reduction) -> ? -> ROS / Mitochondrial ETC -> ? -> Tip Bias
mechanisms.typical_regime: Ionizing dose gradient grad I_gamma + paramagnetic semiquinone centers (g ~ 2.004 ESR signal)
sources: Robertson et al. (2012) PLoS ONE 7(11):e48674 (W. dermatitidis transcriptomics)
Sandia National Laboratories (2024) Cs-137 Fungal Irradiation Report (experimental null caution)
unresolved_questions: Whether radiation-excited melanin transfers electrons to mitochondrial ETC in intact cells
Whether magnetic field vector B alters melanin semiquinone radical-pair recombination yields (tested by Gate 3)

mechanisms.title: System 2 (Route C): Biogenic Magnetite (Fe3O4) Chain Torque Transduction
mechanisms.equation: tau = N_crystals * M_s * V_crystal * B * sin(theta); thermal_gate = tau / (k_B * T) > 1
mechanisms.typical_regime: B = 25 to 65 uT (DC geomagnetic), single-domain Fe3O4 crystals (r ~ 25 nm, chain N = 10 to 20)
sources: Eder et al. (2012) PNAS 109:12022-12027 (contamination controls required)
unresolved_questions: Anatomical identity of primary magnetoreceptor cells and ion-channel tethers in eukaryotes
Distinguishing biogenic intracellular magnetite from exogenous iron oxide contamination

mechanisms.title: System 2 (Marine Reference): Electromagnetic Induction (Ampullae of Lorenzini)
mechanisms.status: ESTABLISHED_IN_ELASMOBRANCHS (requires conductive seawater medium; not intracellular fungal/terrestrial)
mechanisms.equation: EMF = integral (v x B) . dl; E_induced = v * B * sin(theta)
mechanisms.typical_regime: v = 0.2 to 1.0 m/s in seawater (sigma ~ 4 S/m), canal length L = 5 to 20 cm, threshold ~ 5 nV/cm
sources: Newton, Gill & Kajiura (2019) J. R. Soc. Interface 16:20190262
unresolved_questions: Central neural decoding of motional vs. ocean-current induced electric fields

mechanisms.title: System 3: Exogenous MNP Magnetomechanical Torque & Force Gating (Piezo1 / TRPV4)
mechanisms.status: DEMONSTRATED_WITH_SYNTHETIC_MNPS (refuted for endogenous ferritin by Meister 2016)
mechanisms.equation: tau = m x B; F_grad = (m . grad) B; requires F >= 1 to 10 pN or tau >= 40 pN*nm for channel gating
mechanisms.typical_regime: B = 5 to 50 mT (low-frequency rotating/alternating, 1 to 50 Hz) + synthetic Fe3O4 nanodiscs/clusters (r >= 25 to 100 nm)
sources: Meister (2016) eLife 5:e17210 (physical critique of ferritin magnetogenetics)
Gregurec et al. (2020) ACS Nano 14:8036-8045 (vortex nanodisc mechanotransduction)
Lee et al. (2021) Nat. Mater. 20:1029-1036 (m-Torquer nanoscale torque gating)
unresolved_questions: Targeted deep-tissue delivery and stable membrane tethering without immune clearance
Separating pure mechanical gating from local viscous or coil-heating artifacts

mechanisms.title: System 3: RF Magnetothermal Hysteresis Actuation (TRPV1 -> Ca2+ -> Mitochondrial MCU)
mechanisms.equation: P_vol = mu_0 * pi * chi_pp * f * H_0^2; gating TRPV1 (~42 C) triggers Ca2+ -> MCU -> TCA/OXPHOS modulation
mechanisms.typical_regime: f = 100 to 500 kHz, B_RF = 10 to 30 mT; dense MNP clusters required to overcome Fourier heat diffusion
sources: Rabin (2002) Int. J. Hyperthermia 18:194-202 (nano-scale heat transfer bounds)
Chen et al. (2015) Science 347:1477-1480 (magnetothermal deep brain stimulation)
unresolved_questions: Nanoscale surface thermometry vs. macroscopic Fourier heat conduction limits
Preventing mitochondrial Ca2+ overload while modulating metabolic signaling

mechanisms.title: System 3: High-Gradient Vascular SPION Capture & Drug Delivery
mechanisms.status: PRECLINICAL_AND_SUPERFICIAL_TRANSLATION (depth-limited by Earnshaw theorem and gradient decay)
mechanisms.equation: F_mag = V_np * delta_chi * grad(B^2) / (2 * mu_0) vs. F_drag = 6 * pi * eta * r_np * v_blood
mechanisms.typical_regime: B = 0.2 to 1.5 T, |grad B| = 10 to 100 T/m (effective mainly within 1 to 5 cm of magnet pole face)
sources: Pankhurst et al. (2003) J. Phys. D: Appl. Phys. 36:R167
Shapiro et al. (2015) Magn. Reson. Imaging 33:250-256
unresolved_questions: Overcoming Earnshaw's theorem for deep-tissue static magnetic trapping

mechanisms.title: QUARANTINED: 71 THz (4.22 um Mid-IR) Mitochondrial Light-Matter Coupling Preprint
mechanisms.equation: f = 71 THz -> lambda = c / f = 4.22 um (photon energy h*nu = 0.294 eV ~ 11.4 k_B*T)
mechanisms.typical_regime: Mid-infrared vibrational / photonic spectroscopy; NOT geomagnetic DC/ELF sensing
sources: bioRxiv preprint (Sept 2026) on 71 THz cellular/mitochondrial spectral feature (unvalidated)
unresolved_questions: Independent replication with rigorous water/CO2 infrared absorption controls (4.26 um CO2 asymmetric stretch)
No established physical coupling to geomagnetic microtesla fields

preregistration_protocol.primary_outcome: Identified-parcel radial displacement delta_r_i = r_i(t_1) - r_i(t_0) (Null H0-A) contrasted against initial survivor radius r_surv(t_0) (Null H0-B), or circular mean hyphal tip angle theta_tip, with parcel disappearances logged separately.
preregistration_protocol.meoi_and_equivalence_bound: Minimum biologically meaningful effect MEOI = 0.05 r/R (or angular deflection >= 15 deg); two one-sided TOST equivalence tests at alpha = 0.05 (90% CI strictly inside [-MEOI, +MEOI]) and 95% seed-bootstrap intervals (5,000 samples).
preregistration_protocol.dosimetry_and_sham_controls: 3-axis fluxgate magnetometer verification at sample plane; double-wrapped antiparallel Helmholtz sham coils matching thermal dissipation within +/-0.05 C; mechanical vibration isolation; TLD/ion-chamber radiation dose verification.
preregistration_protocol.replicate_and_multiplicity_rules: Blinded plate/chamber randomization, biological replicate blocking across independent inocula, and Holm-Bonferroni familywise error control across separated Movement, Selection, Growth, and Mechanism endpoints.

factorial_experiments.prerequisite_gate: Gate 0 passed (parcel ID tracking, disappearance logging, and sham/temperature controls verified).
factorial_experiments.title: Gate A: Radiation x Melanin Genetics (Separating Selection H0-B from Movement H0-A)
factorial_experiments.factors_varied: Ionizing Radiation (+I_gamma vs. Sham) x Melanin Genotype (WT Melanized vs. Albino Mutant pks1Delta/lac1Delta vs. Complemented Rescue) at fixed, measured ambient geomagnetic field (50 uT)
factorial_experiments.primary_readouts: Separated endpoints: (1) Movement delta_r_i = r_i(t_1) - r_i(t_0) of surviving identified parcels, (2) Selection (parcel survival/death counts & initial survivor radius r_surv(t_0)), (3) Growth (biomass/division), (4) Melanin ESR & NADH reduction
factorial_experiments.discriminating_outcome: Tests Null H0-A & H0-B + Proposition P1: Distinguishes melanin-dependent radioprotection (higher survival near the source) from active radiotropism (non-zero delta_r_i beyond the selection-only counterfactual).

factorial_experiments.prerequisite_gate: Fixed radiation geometry, dose, spectrum, culture media, and temperature controlled (+/-0.05 C), with active double-wrapped sham coils and 3-axis magnetometer verification at the sample.
factorial_experiments.title: Gate B: Magnetic-Field Rotation (+90 deg), Reversal (180 deg) & Suppression (<0.1 uT)
factorial_experiments.factors_varied: Magnetic Field Vector B (Ambient 50 uT vs. Suppressed <0.1 uT vs. +90 deg Rotated vs. 180 deg Reversed vs. Antiparallel Sham Coil) across both Sham (0 Gy) and Fixed Radiation (+grad I_gamma)
factorial_experiments.primary_readouts: Identified-parcel displacement vector delta_r_i / tip angle theta_tip, separate from parcel survival and biomass growth
factorial_experiments.discriminating_outcome: Separates Energy/Mortality Gradient (grad I_gamma) from Directional Information (vector B): Rotation (+90 deg) tests directional cueing orthogonal to the dose gradient; reversal (180 deg) discriminates polarity vs. inclination compasses; suppression (<0.1 uT) tests magnetic necessity.

factorial_experiments.gate_order: Gate 3 (Receptor Identity Gate: Melanin Route A vs. Flavin/Cry Route B)
factorial_experiments.prerequisite_gate: Statistically significant magnetic-field effect on tracked movement/growth established in Gate B relative to sham-energized coils.
factorial_experiments.title: Gate C: Melanin x Magnetic-Field Factorial (Route A vs. Route B)
factorial_experiments.factors_varied: Melanin Genotype (WT Melanized vs. Albino Mutant vs. Complemented Rescue) x Magnetic Field (Baseline, Rotated/Reversed, Suppressed) x Radiation (+/- I_gamma)
factorial_experiments.primary_readouts: Field-dependent shift in tracked delta_r_i / theta_tip and ROS / superoxide (MitoSOX / roGFP2) across WT, Albino, and Rescue genotypes
factorial_experiments.discriminating_outcome: Tests Proposition P2 (Route A vs. Route B): If magnetic-field sensitivity disappears in Albino mutants and is restored in Complemented Rescue, a melanin-dependent route (Route A) is supported. If magnetic sensitivity persists without melanin, flavin/cryptochrome radical-pair chemistry (Route B) operates independently of melanin.

factorial_experiments.prerequisite_gate: Reproducible receptor-linked response established in Gate A, B, or C.
factorial_experiments.title: Gate D: Temporal Ordering (t_mito < t_tip), Pathway Intervention & Phase Null Controls
factorial_experiments.factors_varied: Time-resolved live imaging (t = 0 to 120 min) + Controlled Pathway Intervention (MitoTEMPO / DPI) + Phase Coupling Controls (Uncoupled K = 0 Replay, Phase-Randomized Surrogate, Independent-Oscillator Benchmark)
factorial_experiments.primary_readouts: Lag time between stimulus onset, ROS/redox shift (t_mito), and first detectable tip curvature (t_tip); Kuramoto order parameter R(t) vs. uncoupled K = 0 and phase-shuffled surrogates
factorial_experiments.discriminating_outcome: Tests Propositions P3 & P4: Requires biochemical shift to precede directional growth (t_mito < t_tip) and pathway clamping to abolish the directional response without blocking basal growth. Any oscillatory phase concentration R(t) must exceed uncoupled (K=0), inheritance, and shared-forcing surrogates.

milestones.title: Milestone 1 (Gate 0 & Gate 1): Synthetic Ledger Closure & Selection-vs-Movement Separation
milestones.criterion: Track every parcel ID across time, log disappearances explicitly, close nutrient/biomass budgets (<1e-6), and separate survivor-radius shifts (Null H0-B) from individual parcel displacement delta_r_i (Null H0-A).

milestones.title: Milestone 2 (Gate 2 & Gate 3): Sham-Controlled Magnetic & Genetic Discrimination
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate a B-rotation/reversal/suppression response under sham-coil and sample-plane magnetometer controls, and discriminate melanin dependence (WT/Albino/Rescue) from cryptochrome/flavin chemistry.

milestones.title: Milestone 3 (Gate 4): Temporal Precedence, Causal Intervention & Phase Surrogate Benchmark
milestones.criterion: Prove that redox/mitochondrial signaling precedes and causally mediates directional growth (t_mito < t_tip), and benchmark any phase synchronization R(t) against uncoupled (K=0) and phase-randomized surrogates.
